settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: Both the ExcludedPatterns class (ExcludedPatterns.java lines 4-5, 9) and the commented lines in setExcludeParams (ParametersInterceptor.java lines 510-511) show the fix was intentionally developed, indicating the project considered this a class-access concern.

isAcceptableParameter ANDs acceptableName with any ParameterNameAware check (lines 366-369); acceptableName additionally enforces the length limit and the acceptParams whitelist (lines 411-417, 427-444).
doIntercept sets ReflectionContextState.setDenyMethodExecution(true) before setParameters (lines 236-238), which restricts method invocation during parameter set even if a name is accepted.
struts-default.xml (not re-read in this pass) historically injects an excludeParams value for the params interceptor; if present, the class-access pattern would be excluded at runtime.
candidates.description: In ParametersInterceptor.setExcludeParams (lines 503-513), the intended class-access exclusion pattern is present only inside a comment: line 510 contains `// Patch: Add excludeParams.add(Pattern.compile("(.*\\.|^|.*|\\[('|\"))class(\\.|('|\")]|\\[).*"));` and line 511 is the same call fully commented out. Only caller-supplied `commaDelim` patterns are compiled (lines 504-508). Separately, ExcludedPatterns.EXCLUDED_PATTERNS (ExcludedPatterns.java lines 11-20) defines a hard-coded set (`CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN`, `^dojo\..*`, `^struts\..*`, `^session\..*`, `^request\..*`, `^application\..*`, `^servlet(Request|Response)\..*`, `^parameters\..*`) documented as patterns that "must be rejected by ... ParametersInterceptor", yet no reference to ExcludedPatterns exists anywhere in the reviewed body of ParametersInterceptor (lines 141-515), and isExcluded (446-457) iterates only the injectable excludeParams set. If the exclude pattern is not also supplied through configuration, parameter names such as property paths ending in `class` (e.g. `class.classLoader`) would pass isExcluded and only need to satisfy the accepted name regex at line 145 (`\w+((\.\w+)|(\[\d+\])|(\(\d+\))|(\['\w+'\])|(\(\'\w+\'\)))*`, which allows dots, so `class.classLoader` would match) and line 158. isAcceptableParameter (366-369) then delegates to acceptableName (411-417). This is a candidate for parameter-name-based class access being reachable if no configuration supplies the exclusion, but the actual runtime exclusion set depends on injected configuration that was not read.
missing_evidence: The actual interceptor configuration that feeds excludeParams / acceptParams (struts-default.xml, xwork-default.xml) was only seen as an index excerpt, not read, so the effective excludeParams set is unknown.
Any other class that references ExcludedPatterns.EXCLUDED_PATTERNS and injects it (usage search returned no non-comment reference).
Whether the runtime OGNL/MemberAccessValueStack denies access to `class.classLoader` independently (SecurityMemberAccess, OgnlValueStack, MemberAccessValueStack were not read).
preconditions: ParametersInterceptor is on the interceptor chain for a reachable action (declared in xwork-default.xml per index hit, not re-read here).
A request parameter with a name such as `class.classLoader` (or another class-access path) that satisfies the acceptedPattern at line 145.
No interceptor configuration (struts-default.xml / xwork-default.xml excludeParams, or the ExcludedPatterns list wired in elsewhere) supplies the class-access regex to this interceptor instance.
The action does not implement ParameterNameAware in a way that rejects the name (isAcceptableParameter line 368 would AND it).
candidates.title: ParametersInterceptor: class-access exclusion is commented out; introduced EXCLUDED_PATTERNS list is not applied in this class

counter_evidence: The accepted pattern (line 170) excludes characters commonly needed for OGNL expression syntax such as `#`, parentheses and operators, so the cookie *name* alone is limited to letters/digits/dots/brackets/underscore/apostrophe/whitespace.
The class-access restriction was clearly intended and is referenced in a comment on line 248 and in ExcludedPatterns.java line 5 ("partially in CookInterceptor").

The interceptor javadoc (lines 43-63) states the injection only affects cookies whose name/value are explicitly configured to be injected, and the default cookiesNameSet/cookiesValueSet are empty (lines 172-173), so with default configuration no cookie is injected.
candidates.description: CookieInterceptor.intercept reads all request cookies (line 218) and for each cookie whose name satisfies isAcceptableName calls populateCookieValueIntoStack (lines 226-234). populateCookieValueIntoStack calls `stack.setValue(cookieName, cookieValue)` (line 274 when cookiesValueSet is empty or contains `*`, and line 285 when the value matches the configured set). isAcceptableName (lines 247-250) currently returns `acceptedPattern.matcher(name).matches()`, and the intended exclusion is commented out on line 248: `// Patch: return !Pattern.compile(ExcludedPatterns.CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN).matcher(name).matches();`. The accepted pattern (line 170, `[a-zA-Z0-9\.\]\[_'\s]+`; compiled at line 176) permits dotted property paths such as `class.classLoader`, and the CookieInterceptor does not set ReflectionContextState.DENY_METHOD_EXECUTION nor go through ParametersInterceptor's isAcceptableParameter/acceptableName checks, so the cookie-name filter is the only name gate here. This is a candidate for cookie-name-driven property/class-access on the value stack; whether the resulting setValue can reach security-sensitive state depends on the ValueStack/OGNL layer and on how the interceptor is configured, neither of which was read.
missing_evidence: CookieInterceptor configuration in struts-default.xml / xwork-default.xml (only an index excerpt naming the `cookie` interceptor was seen, not read).
Whether ReflectionContextState.DENY_METHOD_EXECUTION is set on this code path (setValue requires a valid setter/OGNL assignment target).
Behavior of ValueStack.setValue for names like `class.classLoader` (OgnlValueStack, SecurityMemberAccess not read).
preconditions: The cookie interceptor is referenced for the action (not enabled by default; configuration was not read) with cookiesName either `*` or the specific attacker cookie name.
cookiesValue is `*`/empty, or the attacker controls a cookie value that matches the configured cookiesValue set (lines 262, 279).
The action's ValueStack does not independently block `class.classLoader`-style paths (SecurityMemberAccess/OgnlValueStack not read).
candidates.title: CookieInterceptor: attacker-controlled cookie name injected into ValueStack with class-access check commented out

counter_evidence: Both dynamic-method behaviors are explicitly conditional on injected boolean flags that default to false in the reviewed fields (lines 118, 123), and the setter parsing (188-189) uses equalsIgnoreCase on "true".
The class javadoc (lines 54-68) documents these prefixes as intended, documented behavior rather than a defect.
allowedActionNames at line 122 (even with `.` and `!`) restricts the alphabet by excluding `#`, `(`, `)`, `'`, `"` and whitespace, limiting OGNL-injection-shaped names.
candidates.description: DefaultActionMapper defines METHOD_PREFIX = "method:" (line 115) and registers a ParameterAction that, when allowDynamicMethodCalls is true, sets the action method to the substring after the prefix (lines 136-142). It also defines ACTION_PREFIX = "action:" (line 116) and, when allowActionPrefix and allowDynamicMethodCalls are true, extracts the method from the `!` bang syntax (`name.substring(bang + 1)`, lines 144-155) and then sets the action name (line 167). Both behaviors are gated by injected flags: `setAllowDynamicMethodCalls` (188-190, from STRUTS_ENABLE_DYNAMIC_METHOD_INVOCATION) and the `allowActionPrefix` field (line 123) with default false. The default `allowedActionNames` regex compiled at line 122 (`[a-zA-Z0-9._!/\-]*`) permits dots, slashes, bangs and dashes and is a `*` (zero-or-more, unanchored) match that would accept an empty or almost-arbitrary action name; the setter that would install a stricter pattern was only seen as an index excerpt, not read. This is a candidate for dynamic method selection/action-name manipulation reachable from the request URI/hidden field when the corresponding flags are enabled; the security outcome depends on the injected flag values and on the parts of the file beyond line 200 (getMapping/cleanupActionName), which were not read in this pass.
missing_evidence: Default/runtime values of STRUTS_ENABLE_DYNAMIC_METHOD_INVOCATION, STRUTS_ENABLE_SLASHES_IN_ACTION_NAMES, allowActionPrefix and STRUTS_ALLOWED_ACTION_NAMES (default.properties / struts.xml not read).
getMapping, cleanupActionName and the remainder of DefaultActionMapper (lines 201-546) were not read; action-name sanitization there could change the conclusion.
Whether a global interceptor/enforcement layer restricts method invocation at runtime (not read).
preconditions: STRUTS_ENABLE_DYNAMIC_METHOD_INVOCATION resolves to true for `method:` and `!` handling (lines 138, 148); `action:` prefix handling additionally requires allowActionPrefix true (line 146).
The request supplies a URI/hidden field using the `method:`, `action:...!method` or `name!method` syntax.
Any stricter allowedActionNames pattern is not applied, or the requested names still match it.
candidates.title: DefaultActionMapper: dynamic method invocation via `method:` / `action:...!method` prefixes and permissive allowedActionNames regex
